title: Fluids at Rest: Pressure, Buoyancy, and Bernoulli

questions.question: The pressure at a depth h in a liquid at rest depends on:
options: The area of the container's base
questions.rationale: P = P0 + ρgh — pressure at depth grows with depth and density alone; container shape and volume are irrelevant, as communicating vessels show.

questions.question: In a hydraulic press, a 100 N force acts on a piston of area 0.01 m². The pressure lifts a load on a piston of area 0.5 m². The lifting force is:
questions.rationale: P = 100 ÷ 0.01 = 10,000 Pa, so F = P × A₂ = 10,000 × 0.5 = 5,000 N — the force grows by the piston-area ratio A₂/A₁ = 50.

questions.question: Iron has a relative density of about 7.8. This means:
options: Iron is 7.8 times as heavy as air
Iron can hold 7.8 times its weight
Iron is 7.8 times as dense as water
questions.rationale: Relative density is the ratio of a substance's density to water's density, so 7.8 means 7.8 times denser than water — and it carries no unit.

questions.question: A stone weighs 8 N in air and 6.5 N when fully immersed in water. The buoyant force on it is:
questions.rationale: By Archimedes' principle the upthrust equals the loss of weight in the fluid: 8 − 6.5 = 1.5 N, the weight of the displaced water.

questions.question: Roughly nine-tenths of a floating iceberg lies below the surface because:
options: Ice's density is about 0.92 that of water, so that fraction submerges
Ice absorbs water as it melts
questions.rationale: A floating body submerges in the ratio of its density to the fluid's; with relative density about 0.92, about 92% of the iceberg sits below water.

questions.question: A drinking straw raises a drink because of:
options: Atmospheric pressure pushing the liquid up
A vacuum that sucks the liquid
questions.rationale: Sucking lowers the pressure inside the straw; the atmospheric pressure on the drink's surface then pushes the liquid up — a vacuum does not 'suck'.

questions.question: According to Bernoulli's principle, where a fluid flows faster its pressure:
questions.rationale: Faster flow means lower pressure (and slower flow means higher) — valid for streamlined, non-viscous, incompressible flow.

questions.question: An atomiser or perfume sprayer draws liquid up and scatters it because of:
questions.rationale: The bulb speeds air across the tube; the resulting low pressure draws the liquid up into the fast jet, which breaks it into a spray.

questions.question: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted:
options: Only to the bottom of the container
Undiminished to every part of the fluid and the container walls
questions.rationale: An enclosed fluid transmits applied pressure undiminished to all points and walls, acting at right angles — the basis of hydraulic press, brakes, and lifts.

questions.question: An iron ship floats while an iron nail sinks because:
options: Iron becomes less dense in large pieces
Sea water is denser than iron
The ship's hollow shape displaces enough water for the upthrust to match its weight
The nail is lighter than the ship
questions.rationale: Floating depends on average density: the hollow ship's shape displaces a huge volume of water, so the upthrust balances its weight; a solid nail cannot displace enough.
